questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sacred Places and Pilgrimage' refers to.
questions.a: Almost every region of India holds sacred places, temples, mosques, churches, gurdwaras, shrines and tirthas, and journeys to them, called pilgrimage, weave the whole land into one sacred geography.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sacred Places and Pilgrimage'.
questions.a: Sacredness is pinned to place: rivers, hills and shrines become doorways of meaning that millions travel to reach.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sacred Places and Pilgrimage' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Sacred Rivers, Mountains and Groves' refers to.
questions.a: Nature itself is revered: the Ganga and other rivers are worshipped as mothers, mountains like Kailash and Govardhan held holy, and trees, plants and sacred groves protected by villages across the land.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sacred Rivers, Mountains and Groves'.
questions.a: Reverence for nature is conservation in cultural dress: a sacred river or grove is guarded by faith, not fences.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sacred Rivers, Mountains and Groves' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'The Elements as One Body' refers to.
questions.a: The Bhagavata Purana verse sees ether, air, fire, water, earth, planets, creatures, directions, trees, rivers and seas as organs of the supreme Lord's body, teaching that harming nature is harming the divine itself.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Elements as One Body'.
questions.a: When the world is the body of the sacred, every element deserves respect.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Elements as One Body' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Sharing Across Faiths: Debates and Festivals

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sharing Across Faiths: Debates and Festivals' refers to.
questions.a: Sacred places grew into meeting grounds: discussions and debates, sharing of goods and experiences, festivals and fairs where communities of every faith met, traded and learned from one another.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sharing Across Faiths: Debates and Festivals'.
questions.a: Sacred geography is social geography: the same shrine feeds faith, friendship and commerce together.
